teams.heading: Maddie Feaunati returns to England Women's side for New Zealand Test
teams.body: Maddie Feaunati returns to the back row for England Women this weekend as the team prepares to face New Zealand at Allianz Stadium. Head coach John Mitchell confirmed Feaunati will start at number eight, with Alex Matthews moving to blind-side flanker and Abi Burton rotating to the bench. Following a 26-26 draw against Canada, Mitchell remains optimistic: "Test matches against the best teams in the world are what we relish and look forward to, especially at Allianz Stadium."

teams.heading: Caelan Doris remains Leinster captain but faces November international fitness doubt
teams.body: Leinster head coach Leo Cullen has confirmed that Caelan Doris will continue as club captain this season, but his availability for Ireland’s upcoming Nations Championship matches remains uncertain. Doris has been sidelined following surgery on a knee injury sustained during the URC final, with his rehabilitation progress currently delayed. Cullen admitted he is "not 100 per cent sure" on the timeline for a return, casting doubt on whether the forward will be match-fit for the November Test series against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa.

teams.heading: Italy Men prepare for Nations Championship clash at Allianz Stadium venue
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada’s side will return to Turin in November to face world champions South Africa, marking the team’s first home fixture in the inaugural Nations Championship. Across their last 11 outings, the Azzurri have scored 190 points and conceded 318, with their largest victory in that window remaining the 34-19 win against Chile at home in November 2025.

teams.heading: Darcy Graham Ruled Out Of Scotland Autumn Tests With Ruptured Bicep
teams.body: Scotland and Edinburgh have suffered a major setback after Darcy Graham was ruled out for a minimum of 12 weeks with a ruptured bicep. Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt confirmed that the winger picked up the injury during a friendly collision against Harlequins, missing the scan results initially before a Monday MRI confirmed the tear. The 29-year-old will miss the upcoming November Tests against New Zealand, Australia and Japan at Murrayfield, alongside the initial part of the club season.

teams.heading: Harry Bowcott emerges as frontrunner to become new WRU chair
teams.body: Former McKinsey senior partner Harry Bowcott has emerged as the frontrunner to become the next chairman of the Welsh Rugby Union following interviews at the Sport Wales office in Cardiff. The 51-year-old Cambridge graduate, whose late grandfather Henry Morgan Bowcott played for Wales and served as WRU president, is competing against former Harlequins chief executive Mark Evans for the independent non-executive role. The successful candidate will oversee the board's plans to reduce Wales' professional teams from four to three.

teams.heading: Pumas Hammer Iberians As Tino Swanepoel Crosses Five Times
teams.body: The Pumas recorded an emphatic 64-21 victory over Spain's Iberians in Tbilisi, having established a commanding 40-14 lead at half-time. Left wing Tino Swanepoel was the star of the show, crossing five times as the side ran in 10 tries in total. Clinton Swart, Wian van Niekerk, Gustav du Rand, Alfondso Isaacs and André Fouché also crossed the whitewash, with Swart adding 5 conversions alongside 2 from Bradley Giddy.

teams.heading: Les Kiss names Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the wing for Springboks Test
teams.body: Les Kiss has named Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to start on the left wing for the first time in his Test career ahead of Sunday's fixture against South Africa in Perth. The code-hopper moves from the centres to the outside backs where his aerial ability can be utilised, with Hunter Paisami returning to partner Len Ikitau in the midfield. Kiss has also changed tack by selecting a 6-2 forward-heavy bench split to match the world champions, having stated: "We've had a solid preparation window here in Perth ahead of what's going to be a massive Test against South Africa."

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One Relents On Contentious Foreign Player Registration
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has backtracked on contentious new player registration rules following a fierce backlash from fans and players that saw 27 individuals file a complaint with the Japan Fair Trade Commission. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji acknowledged shortcomings in the league's handling of the issue, stating, "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes. We would like to reflect on that." Under the revised system, foreign-born players who acquired citizenship by May 2025 will be treated as Japanese-born players.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus Explains Wholesale Changes and Springboks Squad Overhaul in Perth
teams.body: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has defended his decision to make 13 changes to his starting line-up for Sunday's clash against the Wallabies in Perth. The world champions' starting XV features 355 fewer caps than the side that defeated New Zealand, with Erasmus explaining that the wholesale rotation was necessary after leaning heavily on a core of 24 players during the recent series. "There's always a balance between fans and the media; you need to understand that we're building to the World Cup, and we are trying to win between World Cups, and sometimes you have to roll the dice," Erasmus said.
